tasks.short: Review orders and confirm prescribed MRI examinations

steps.what: Review physicians' orders, resolve discrepancies and confirm the prescribed exams

tasks.design: Keep order review and examination confirmation with the technologist in the existing {OTHER} radiology information system. Native order display supports the review, but no model chooses or changes the prescribed examination.
tasks.previous_blocker: The actual order and examination context must agree, and discrepancies need clinical clarification.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing radiology order access supports review without establishing a new labour saving.
tasks.still_hard: Recognise an unclear or inconsistent request and obtain clarification before confirming it.
tasks.human_edge: Notice a mismatch that a complete set of fields could still conceal.
tasks.altitude: Order-review responsibilities and authority remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Separate identifying an order discrepancy from changing the clinical request.

evidence.claim: Reviewing and confirming a prescribed examination is contextual clinical work, distinct from selecting an imaging protocol from a list.

assumptions: Boundary is order review and confirmation, excluding protocol selection, patient safety screening, image acquisition and diagnosis.

OTHER is the existing radiology information system. The physician produces the order with patient reference, requested examination, anatomical area and clinical question before s1; scheduling staff produce the scheduled examination in their existing workflow. The technologist reads and checks the actual records in retained s1 time.
Missing or conflicting information produces a clarification request, not an inferred confirmation flag. Existing physician clarification time remains unchanged outside the focal denominator.
No new system, integration or capture duty is introduced. Native order access is sufficient and incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Existing order confirmation and escalation process
research_questions: Which order discrepancies most often require physician clarification?

already_counted.description: All review, clarification and examination confirmation remains.

approvals.approved_version: Exact physician order version, patient reference, scheduled examination and confirmed examination reviewed in s1; any change voids confirmation.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Existing order-display runtime is not newly saved review labour.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Conduct screening interviews of patients using the current local MRI safety questions
Clarify reported contraindications and record unresolved safety concerns for the authorised review route

tasks.design: Keep patient screening interviews and clarification human, recording findings in the existing {OTHER} radiology information system. Use the current local screening procedure without treating a questionnaire as automatic clearance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Patients may not know the details needed to interpret a screening answer safely.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing screening guidance supports the interview but does not remove clarification.
tasks.still_hard: Recognise uncertainty and obtain the appropriate authorised safety review.
tasks.human_edge: Ask follow-up questions and avoid converting an unknown answer into an assumed negative.
tasks.altitude: Screening duties and safety decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Record uncertainty explicitly and use the established escalation route.

evidence.claim: Patient screening requires eliciting and clarifying actual answers; structured questionnaire completion alone does not establish safety.

assumptions: Boundary is the screening interview and its record, excluding final specialist safety clearance, device assessment and the general medical-history task.

The local safety owner supplies current questions before s1. Patients produce their answers during s1, and the technologist captures answers and uncertainties during s2; no free contraindication or clearance flag is presumed.
OTHER is the existing radiology information system. Uncertain information follows the existing manual review route; its unchanged specialist work remains outside the focal denominator.
No new tool, recording or data-entry transfer is introduced. Native screening records are sufficient and incremental upkeep is zero. Any overlapping history question is asked once in a team roll-up.
unknowns: Current local screening and authorised review responsibilities
research_questions: Which questions most often require clarification rather than a simple yes or no answer?

already_counted.description: Interview, clarification and screening record remain.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=70+30=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. No patient interview or safety clarification is automated.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Provide headphones or earplugs for patient comfort

steps.what: Provide headphones or earplugs and check the patient's fit and comfort

tasks.design: Keep provision and fit checking with the technologist. Existing equipment guidance in {DOCS} supports the physical work without replacing direct patient assistance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Hearing protection must be physically supplied and checked with the patient.
tasks.enabler_now: Reference access does not perform fitting or establish comfort.
tasks.still_hard: Adapt assistance to the patient and resolve an uncomfortable or unsuitable fit.
tasks.human_edge: Observe the actual fit and listen to the patient's feedback.
tasks.altitude: Patient comfort and physical assistance duties remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Check fit and comfort directly rather than assuming completion.

evidence.claim: Providing and checking hearing protection is physical patient assistance and is not performed by a digital record.

assumptions: Boundary is providing locally approved protection and checking fit and comfort, excluding procurement and separate equipment cleaning tasks.
Existing equipment owners provide approved supplies and guidance before s1; the technologist observes fit and gathers patient feedback during s1. No free fit or comfort flag is assumed.
No new system, capture obligation or upkeep is introduced. Native document access is sufficient and incremental work is zero.
research_questions: Which fit problems require additional patient assistance?

already_counted.description: All physical provision and comfort checking remains.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. No physical assistance is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Take brief medical histories from patients and clarify uncertain or conflicting information

tasks.design: Keep the brief history conversation with the technologist, using authorised existing context from the {OTHER} clinical record system. Do not substitute an old record or generated summary for checking the patient's current account.
tasks.previous_blocker: Current history must be elicited and clarified with the patient.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records support questions but do not eliminate the conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Resolve incomplete recollection and differences between the current account and prior records.
tasks.human_edge: Listen for uncertainty and ask a useful follow-up question.

reach.learn: Separate confirmed information from uncertainty and clarify conflicts.

evidence.claim: The Dutch general-practice ambient-scribe study reported reduced documentation time with unchanged consultation length; it does not establish a saving in MRI history-taking.

assumptions: Boundary is eliciting a brief general history, excluding separate screening, formal documentation production and diagnosis. Any question overlapping safety screening is asked once in a roll-up.

The patient provides current history during s1. Existing clinical staff produced any prior record in their normal care workflow; the technologist checks relevant context and clarifies gaps in retained s1 time. No free structured current-history input is presumed.
OTHER is the existing clinical record system. Uncertain facts remain explicit and follow existing clarification routes; no new recording, summary service or capture duty is introduced.
Native record access is sufficient and incremental upkeep is zero because the workflow is unchanged.
unknowns: Current history scope and access to prior records
research_questions: Which conflicts between patient accounts and existing records most often require follow-up?

already_counted.description: All current-history questioning and clarification remains.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Documentation-study savings are outside the history-taking conversation and are not reused here.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The technologist retains order review, screening, physical assistance and history-taking; no time reduction is claimed for these patient-facing duties.
reach: Clarify patient information and unresolved questions with clinical colleagues through existing routes.
role.ambitious_version: Provide careful, responsive patient support while retaining existing clinical authority and direct human checks.
